question: Does the 2005 Butas River migratory-fish paper expose source-resolved species or event data for Bangwit's freshwater coverage?

source.title: Assessment of migratory fishes in Butas River, Naujan, Oriental Mindoro, Philippines
source.author: Marilyn Martinez Alcanices
source.publication: In Proceedings of the First National Congress on Philippine Lakes, pp. 72-76
source.publisher: Southeast Asian Regional Center for Graduate Study and Research in Agriculture (SEARCA)
source.access: SEAFDEC repository metadata and abstract were reviewed. The item page lists no associated files. The proceedings catalogue lists the paper among poster presentations and links externally to SEARCA; the full paper was not retrieved.

survey.frequency: Fish samples collected once per month
survey.stationResult: The abstract reports mullet, milkfish and caranx at Stations 1 and 4; it does not give binomials, counts, sample dates per taxon, voucher identifiers or coordinates.

limitations: The source is an abstract in repository metadata; the five-page conference paper was not available as an item file.
Common names do not uniquely identify species. Do not assign scientific names to mullet, milkfish, or caranx based on this abstract alone.
Station barangays are not coordinates or precise river reaches, and the abstract does not state taxon-specific station counts beyond the two endpoint stations.
The report's 2003 findings are historical and cannot be used as current presence, abundance, catchability, fishing guidance or a present legal warning.
No item-specific reuse license or public-app projection permission was found in the reviewed metadata.

rightsAndUse.decision: Retain only bibliographic and attributed abstract-level research notes. Do not reproduce the full paper, derive species rows, or project a current Butas River warning from the abstract.

sources.supports: Author, publication year, citation, abstract, four stations, 2003 sample period, gear, and reported common-name fish groups; the item page says no files are associated.
Proceedings metadata, page range, and listing of the paper in the poster presentations; repository page links externally to SEARCA.
SEARCA publisher catalogue entry for the 2005 First National Congress on Philippine Lakes proceedings.

nextAction: Search for an accessible publisher or library copy of the proceedings without purchasing or requesting a scan. If obtained, verify the station table, taxonomic identifications and reuse terms before crosswalking any fish names. Continue MIMAROPA freshwater coverage separately from current local presence claims.
